hypothesis: A dedicated Language Mediation family and an explicit plainspoken-input gate prevent an exact language-pair skill from silently combining specialist-register interpretation with regional-language translation.

evidence.finding: Register mediation and regional-language translation must be two distinct serial skill invocations.
The former generic multi-target webpage-localization package conflicts with exact-pair terminology and controlled composition.

changes.change: Moved the package from universal to language-mediation.
changes.benefit: Family discovery now reflects its shared language, locale, and register-governance role.
changes.risk: Existing links to the Universal path must migrate.

changes.change: Raised the package to 1.1.0 and required a plainspoken en-US input or completed register-mediation record.
changes.risk: Technical-source requests now block until an upstream mediation skill exists.

changes.change: Added a serial-mediation evaluation case and marked the 1.0.0 review historical.
changes.benefit: The current package does not inherit an obsolete family-placement claim.
changes.risk: No independent or native-language quality evidence is added.

decision: retain the exact-pair package as the first language-mediation family member; purge the generic multi-target webpage-localization concept rather than relocate it.
limitations: This ledger records an architectural and structural change only.
No medical, legal, engineering, or other register-mediation package is created by this change.
No translation-quality, native-review, or live-automation claim is established.
